series_label: 河西走廊历史阅读 · 连载 05
title_en: Names, Grain, and Messages: A Han Frontier in Wooden Slips
title_zh: 姓名、粮食与文书：居延汉简中的边塞日常
lead: 一枚木简能留住一名驻卒的名字；另一枚记下粮食与交接，带我们走近边塞的日常。

paragraphs.en: A wooden register from the Han frontier records the names, home places, and ages of soldiers posted far from home. Another records grain received by a garrison unit. These are modest pieces of wood, but they answer the question left by yesterday’s article: what kept a newly organized border working after the campaigns of 121 BCE? The answer was repeated, accountable work. We can follow it at Juyan, north of the main Hexi oasis route, where the Han built a network tied to Zhangye Commandery. Juyan is one case, not a complete portrait of every Hexi post. Its surviving slips make the demands of distance unusually visible.
paragraphs.zh: 一份汉代边塞名簿记下了远离家乡的驻卒姓名、籍贯和年龄。另一份记下了一支驻军领取的粮食。这些木片看似平凡，却能回答上一篇留下的问题：公元前121年战事之后，新建的边境体系靠什么持续运转？答案是反复进行、需要核对的劳动。我们可以沿河西绿洲主道以北的居延追查；汉朝在那里建立了与张掖郡相连的边塞网络。居延是一例，不能代表河西每一处驻地；但其保存下来的汉简，让遥远距离带来的要求格外清晰。

paragraphs.en: The first requirement was knowing who was there. The Juyan soldiers’ registers held by Academia Sinica list individual names, native places, and ages. Scholars have grouped several fragments because the handwriting resembles one another and the men’s native places all point to Zhangye Commandery. A register did not tell a commander what each man felt about service. It did make people countable and identifiable within a chain of command. Behind each entry was a person whose labor could be assigned to a watchtower, a journey, or another duty. The slip preserves the state’s view of him, while also preventing us from seeing the garrison as an anonymous mass.
paragraphs.zh: 第一项要求是知道谁在那里。中央研究院所藏的居延驻卒名簿，逐人列出姓名、籍贯与年龄。研究者依据相近的笔迹，以及这些人的籍贯都指向张掖郡，把若干残简归为同一册的可能性较高。名簿不会告诉长官每个人怎样看待服役，却能让人在指挥链中被计数、被辨认。每条记录背后，都是可能被派去守烽燧、出行或承担其他任务的人。木简保存的是国家观看他的角度，同时也让我们不必把驻军看成没有面目的整体。

paragraphs.en: The second requirement was food. At the Wansui platoon near Juyan, a granary register dated to 2 BCE includes a title slip and entries for grain distribution to officials and soldiers. The museum identifies several pieces as parts of a bound volume. Names of recipients and repeated quantities matter here more than any dramatic event: they show that rations had to be measured and recorded. Grain did not simply appear because a fort had been built. It had to be grown or brought in, stored, issued, and checked. The register documents distribution at one unit; it does not reveal every field, carrier, or household involved in supplying it.
paragraphs.zh: 第二项要求是粮食。居延附近万岁部的一册粮食簿，年代为公元前2年，包括题名简和向官兵发粮的记录。博物馆把其中几枚认定为同一编册的组成部分。领粮人的名字与反复出现的数量，比任何戏剧性事件都更重要：口粮需要计量、登记。营垒建成后，粮食不会自行出现；它必须经过种植或运入、储存、发放与核对。这本簿册记录的是一支部队的分粮，无法告诉我们参与供应的每块田地、每名运送者或每户人家。

paragraphs.en: The third requirement was moving information. Two fragments of a post register from the Juyan region record successive dates in the sixth month. According to the museum’s analysis, Han postal delivery used stages: each section noted the kind and number of documents, when they arrived and departed, and who handled them. Delivery had a time limit. A message could cross a long frontier only because someone accepted responsibility for one part of its route and passed it onward. This was a practical answer to distance, but it also created a record of delay and responsibility. The surviving pieces do not let us follow one particular message all the way to its destination.
paragraphs.zh: 第三项要求是传递消息。居延地区两枚驿递簿残简，分别记着六月中相接的两个日期。按博物馆的研究，汉代文书分段递送：每一段记录文书种类与数量、收发时间，以及经手者，并有交付时限。一份消息之所以能穿越漫长边境，是因为有人负责其中一段路，接收后再交给下一段。这是应对距离的实际办法，也留下了延误与责任的记录。现存残片不足以让我们追踪某一份文书直到终点。

paragraphs.en: Wood itself shaped this system. Before paper became the usual writing surface, officials wrote on slips and sometimes bound several together. The Juyan finds include different forms made mostly from local woods; strings that held volumes together often decayed, leaving separate pieces for modern researchers to compare. Writing, binding, carrying, storing, and eventually discarding these records all took time and material. A slip could be reused, cut down, or burned as fuel. What survives is therefore a selection created by loss as well as preservation. Historians reconstruct a working archive from fragments, and a neat modern account must not hide that uncertainty.
paragraphs.zh: 木材本身也塑造了这套制度。在纸成为常用书写材料之前，官员写在简牍上，有时把多枚编在一起。居延出土物包含不同形制，材料多为当地木材；编绳常已朽坏，留下分散的简片，供今天的研究者比较。书写、编联、传送、存放，最后丢弃这些记录，都消耗时间和材料。木简也可能被再利用、削去旧字，或作为燃料烧掉。因此，幸存材料既是保存的结果，也是损失后的残余。历史学家从残片重建运作中的档案，流畅的现代叙述不能掩盖其中的不确定性。

paragraphs.en: The records also show the unequal reach of our evidence. A soldier’s name may survive because an office needed to register him; the work of someone who planted grain, drove a cart, repaired a wall, or lived near the post may leave a different trace or none at all. We should not turn an official list into a complete social history. Nor should we assume every resident belonged to the same group. Han frontier administration operated among soldiers, settlers, and communities already living around the corridor and its northern approaches. The documents clarify what officials counted. They do not settle how all those people understood or negotiated the new order.
paragraphs.zh: 这些记录也显示了证据覆盖范围的不均。士兵的名字可能因官署需要登记而留存；种粮、赶车、修墙，或住在驻地附近的人，可能留下别种痕迹，也可能全无痕迹。我们不能把官方名单当成完整的社会史，也不能假定所有居民属于同一人群。汉代边塞行政运行于士兵、移民，以及早已生活在河西走廊和北部周边的社群之间。文书能说明官员计量了什么，却不能解决所有人如何理解或应对新秩序的问题。

paragraphs.en: Juyan also helps us distinguish a frontier network from a single road. It lay along the northern reaches connected with Zhangye, while Dunhuang’s western defenses formed another part of the wider system. The International Dunhuang Programme describes forts, storehouses, beacon towers, and Han wooden documents along the Dunhuang frontier. These places were not identical, and their records come from different times. Read together with care, they show why a line of forts needed more than walls: people had to receive food, record supplies, move messages, and maintain equipment. The network linked places through duties that had to be performed again and again.
paragraphs.zh: 居延也帮助我们分清边塞网络与单一道路。它位于联系张掖的北部地带；敦煌以西的防线则是更大体系的另一部分。国际敦煌项目介绍了敦煌边塞的堡垒、仓储设施、烽燧与汉代木简。这些地点并不相同，留下的文书也不属于同一时期。谨慎地合看，它们说明一列营垒为何不能只靠墙体维持：人们还要领粮、记录物资、传递消息、维护器具。各处通过一次又一次履行的职责连接起来。

paragraphs.en: This is the turn in the story after conquest. In the previous article, commanderies and guarded routes took shape gradually; at Juyan, the paperwork exposes some of the labor inside that process. A registered soldier, a measured grain issue, and a timed handover were small acts with large consequences. If they failed, a distant post could lose food or information even while its walls remained standing. The surviving slips prove that such routines were recorded, not that they always succeeded. They make the frontier less abstract: holding territory depended on ordinary people doing repeated tasks under difficult conditions, not on a campaign’s victory alone.
paragraphs.zh: 这就是战事之后，故事发生转向的地方。上一篇写郡与设防道路逐渐成形；在居延，文书揭示了这一过程内部的一部分劳作。登记一名士兵、计量一份口粮、按时交接文书，都是看似细小却后果重大的行动。倘若失误，即使墙还立着，偏远驻地也可能失去粮食或消息。幸存汉简证明这些程序曾被记录，不能证明它们总能成功。边疆因此不再只是抽象的地名：维持控制，依靠的是普通人在艰难条件下反复完成的任务，而不只是一次战役的胜利。

paragraphs.en: The slips leave one further question. They are strongest on what offices demanded: names, quantities, dates, and handlers. They are weaker on the relationships that formed around those demands. The next step in this series can follow a specific, well-documented encounter at a Hexi relay station, where official records show how travelers, hosts, and supplies met. For today, Juyan supplies a complete answer to the narrower question. A Han border endured through a chain of registered people, measured provisions, and documented handovers. The wood has survived unevenly; the labor it records was once continuous.
paragraphs.zh: 汉简还留下一个问题。它们最清楚地呈现官署的要求：姓名、数量、日期与经手者；对围绕这些要求形成的人际关系，所能说明的则较少。本系列下一步可追踪河西某处有充分文书证据的驿站接待事件，看看行旅、接待者与物资如何相遇。就今天较窄的问题而言，居延已经给出完整答案：汉代边境靠登记在册的人、计量过的供给，以及留有记录的交接串联而延续。木片的保存很不均衡；它们记下的劳作，当年却必须持续进行。

questions.q: What three kinds of routine work do the Juyan slips document?
questions.a: They document registering soldiers, measuring and distributing grain, and recording the staged handover of documents.

questions.q: Why can the Juyan records not describe every person on the Han frontier?
questions.a: They were made for official needs, survive only in fragments, and leave much work and many local people outside the written record.

questions.q: How does Juyan continue the previous article’s account of Han commanderies?
questions.a: It shows some of the repeated labor—registration, provisions, and communication—that allowed the developing frontier system to function.
